claim: For the Liu–Tan memory-based prey-taxis predator–prey model, Theorem 3.1(a)'s printed parameter shortcut is false when the algebraic lower bound \(L\) is negative. With \(r=K=m=\beta=\gamma=\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta_3=A=1\), \(\alpha=2\), \(\gamma_1=2\), and \(\eta=1/10\), all parameters are positive, \(r>\beta_1\eta\), the paper's weak-Allee condition \(\gamma_1>\beta_2\) holds, and \(\beta<C_1\); nevertheless the reduced coexistence polynomial is \(f(u)=-u^2-u/5-341/100\), which has no positive root and therefore no root in the actual admissible interval \((L_0,U)=(0,9/10)\). The source's proof itself uses \(L_0=\max\{0,L\}\), whereas the theorem statement and its parameter shortcuts use \(L\); the sign-change criterion must be applied at \(L_0\), not at a negative, biologically inadmissible \(L\).
integrity: All numerical values in the counterexample are exact rationals derived from the published equilibrium formulas. The source's primary MSC and publication date were verified from the publisher record; no independence beyond same-model review is claimed.
scientific_limitations: The result disproves the printed parameter shortcut only in the regime where \(L<0\) and identifies the endpoint correction required by the sign-change proof. It does not supply a complete new multiplicity theorem, does not assess nonhomogeneous equilibria, and does not invalidate later analyses at parameter choices where the positive equilibrium has been independently established.
title: A positive-parameter counterexample to a coexistence shortcut in a prey-taxis model
